name: Function Components
description: A JavaScript function that accepts a single `props` object and returns JSX describing what should render on screen. This is the standard way to define components in modern React.
parameters: props — an object of values passed down from the parent component.
returns: A React element (JSX) or, in newer React versions, other renderable values like strings, numbers, arrays, or null.
notes: Function components can use Hooks (useState, useEffect, etc.); class components cannot use Hooks.

name: JSX
description: A syntax extension to JavaScript that lets you write HTML-like markup inside JS files. It compiles to `React.createElement()` calls under the hood.
returns: A React element (a plain JS object describing the DOM node to render).
notes: Use `className` instead of `class`, and camelCase for most DOM attributes (e.g. `onClick`, `tabIndex`).

name: Fragments (<>...</>)
description: Lets a component return multiple sibling elements without adding an extra wrapper node to the DOM.
returns: A grouped list of children with no additional DOM element.
notes: Use the explicit `<React.Fragment key={id}>` form (instead of the `<>` shorthand) when you need to pass a `key`, such as inside a mapped list.

name: children Prop
description: A special prop that holds whatever is nested between a component's opening and closing tags, enabling components to wrap and render arbitrary content.
returns: Whatever was passed as nested JSX — a single element, a string, an array of elements, or nothing.
notes: children can be any renderable value, so guard against unexpected types when rendering it directly.

name: Composition vs Inheritance
description: React recommends composing components (nesting and passing props/children) to share and reuse behavior rather than building class inheritance hierarchies.
notes: The official React docs state they have not found a use case where an inheritance hierarchy is recommended over composition.

name: Conditional Rendering
description: Rendering different JSX depending on a condition, typically with ternaries, `&&`, early returns, or if/else outside the JSX.
returns: The JSX for whichever branch is truthy/selected; null or false renders nothing.
notes: Avoid `{count && <Badge />}` when `count` can be `0` — it renders the literal `0` instead of nothing; use `count > 0 && ...` instead.

name: Rendering Lists with key
description: Rendering an array of data as a list of elements using `.map()`, giving each element a stable `key` so React can track identity across re-renders.
parameters: key — a string/number unique among siblings, used by React's reconciliation algorithm.
notes: Avoid using array index as `key` when the list can reorder, be filtered, or have items inserted/removed — it can cause state and DOM to mismatch.

name: Controlled Components
description: A form element whose value is driven entirely by React state, updated via an `onChange` handler, making state the single source of truth.
notes: Controlled inputs make validation, formatting, and conditional disabling straightforward since every keystroke updates state.

name: Uncontrolled Components
description: A form element that manages its own state internally in the DOM; React reads its current value on demand via a ref instead of tracking every change.
notes: Useful for simple forms, file inputs (which can't be controlled), or integrating with non-React code; less predictable than controlled components.

name: Presentational vs Container Components
description: A pattern separating components that focus on how things look (presentational, mostly props-driven) from components that focus on how things work (container, manage state/data-fetching).
notes: Largely superseded by custom hooks in modern React, which extract stateful logic without requiring a wrapper component.
